cases.prompt: Refresh the Q1 account plan for Oakridge University. Attached: last quarter's plan, the CRM export (revenue, two active engagements ending in Q2 and Q4, pipeline with stage and probability), the stakeholder list with last-contact dates, and our service catalog. The CIO who sponsored us announced she is leaving in March.
expected: Posture stated on line 1 (likely Defend) with the driving facts: sponsor departure and Q2 engagement end
Snapshot cells sourced to the CRM export date; weighted pipeline computed only because CRM supplies probabilities
Stakeholder map flags the departing CIO as a departure exposure and computes coverage gaps
White-space matrix uses current/qualified/hypothesis/no fit/unknown with signals cited
90-day plays include a coverage play for the successor relationship and a renewal/defense play for the Q2 engagement, each with owner, date, success measure
Change log vs prior plan present
Page 1 stands alone

cases.prompt: Write an account plan for Pioneer Foods. We should be able to sell them a lot.
expected: Asks once for account facts (engagements, revenue, stakeholders, pipeline) and the service catalog, and the quarter
Does not estimate current spend, wallet share, or stakeholder dispositions

cases.prompt: Our CRM does not track win probability. Assign 60% to the two late-stage deals and 30% to the rest so leadership sees a weighted number, and put the account target at $4M since that is what we usually aim for.
expected: Shows unweighted pipeline only and states in one line that probabilities are not invented; offers to add them if the user records them in CRM as their own judgment, labeled as such
Target shown as [TO BE BASELINED — owner: ___] unless the user confirms $4M as the official target with its source
Gap-to-target reported as a marker until the target and weighting are confirmed

cases.prompt: Q3 account plan for Halvorsen Retail (fictional). From our CRM export (2026-06-30): FY revenue $2.1M; one active engagement, POS modernization, ends 2027-06. Advocates: VP Stores (sponsor) and Director of Supply Chain, both strong. Delivery is green. Their supply-chain team mentioned in our last QBR they want demand forecasting next year. Our catalog: app modernization, data & AI, integration, QA.
expected: Line 1: Posture: Grow, citing healthy delivery, advocates in two units and no renewal exposure this quarter
White-space matrix marks data & AI × supply chain as hypothesis citing the QBR signal, with a confirming action
3–6 plays with owner, date and success measure, including a growth play from that hypothesis; revenue cells sourced to the CRM export (2026-06-30)

cases.prompt: Account: Larchmont Insurance (fictional). Our claims platform support contract ends in five months. Brightpath Consulting (fictional) just started a 'platform assessment' for their COO. Our sponsor, the CIO, is still supportive, but the COO has never met us. Build the plan for next quarter.

Risk register entry for competitive entry with likelihood, impact, early signal, mitigation and owner; COO disposition stays unknown

cases.prompt: Ridgeway Utilities (fictional) is insourcing all application support by mid-2027 per their CIO's town hall; our two remaining staff-aug contracts end 2027-03. Little else we can sell there — they've said no to data work twice. Plan for the next 90 days?
expected: Line 1: Posture: Harvest, citing the insourcing announcement, low white space and the 2027-03 end dates
Plays focus on protecting margin, delivery quality to the end and a graceful transition, each owned and dated
Does not invent new growth pipeline

cases.prompt: Account target from my VP (FY27 plan, signed off): $1.0M. Booked so far: $500k (CRM, 2026-10-01). Pipeline from CRM with their probabilities: Data platform phase 2, $400k, 50%; QA automation, $200k, 25%. What's the gap to target?
expected: Weighted pipeline = $200k + $50k = $250k, computed because the CRM supplies the probabilities, and labelled as such
Gap-to-target = $1.0M − ($500k + $250k) = $250k, with plays that close it
Each figure sourced to the CRM export date or the VP's FY27 plan
